_comment: Pool eviction policy — the operator's standing decisions, codified once so enforcement is deterministic (ccache semantics: bounded cache, automatic eviction). Consumed by pool-lib.sh enforce_pool / cargo-pool enforce, the SessionStart/Stop hooks, the cargo-disk-guard PreToolUse hook, and .husky/pre-push pressure strategy. Decided 2026-06-04 (operator-confirmed: merge-aware dispositions, 150G/75/85 budget, full gate enforcement). Evidence basis: genesis/docs — 71% of the pool was stale ~1GB DWARF test binaries; see memory project_rust_build_footprint_anatomy.
_keep_warm_slot_days: keep-warm trim survivors: the freshest slot per crate (workspace key) built within this many days is always kept; colder keys become candidates oldest-first. Per-slot operator pin: `touch <slot>/.pin` (e.g. the fork conductor — ~3G, ~45 min rebuild).
_evidence_2026_08_28: The pool is a cluster-stability control, not only disk hygiene: the workspace PV lives on the root fs of the host that runs the only k8s control plane; a netconsole trace (2026-08-28 23:00Z) showed kswapd soft-locked in ext4_es_scan/__es_shrink (extent-status shrinker, cost ∝ inode count + fragmentation) — 14 CPUs followed, cluster API down for hours, 17th freeze. The pool held 341K of the PV's ~1.02M inodes (126G) and its churn fragments the extent tree. Two enforcement gaps let it grow: hash-gc and the keep-warm cap both skipped the ACTIVE family (dev sat at 96G under a 60G cap). Both now apply slot-granularly with in-use/pin guards.

_dispositions.evict-on-merge: auto-evicted when EVERY local+remote branch under <family>/* is merged into dev AND no live worktree/PIDs reference the family. Active session's family is always protected regardless.
_dispositions.keep-warm: never evicted as a family — and trimmed to max_gb EVEN WHILE ACTIVE (the active family is the one that grows; a cap that pauses during work never binds). Survivors: freshest slot per crate built within keep_warm_slot_days, pinned (<slot>/.pin), linked, and in-use slots (cargo lock held or a live process executing from the slot). Candidates go release-profile-first, then oldest-first. Unmeetable caps are reported, never forced.
_dispositions.ttl: evicted after ttl_days with no filesystem activity anywhere in the family tree.

ram._comment: RAM guard policy (genesis/agentic/bin/ram-guard + .claude/hooks/ram-guard.py). Percentages are of the container cgroup memory.max (devfile memoryLimit) measured on COMMITTED memory (anon+kernel+shmem+unevictable — page cache is reclaimable and not counted). Evidence 2026-08-29 17:12Z: the pod had memory.oom.group=1 so one OOM event killed all 35 processes + PID 1; trigger = rustc 4.3G + 7 rust-lld on top of 3 conductors (~1.2G RSS each). soft = advisory; high = shed newest compile tree + deny new heavy builds; hard = tier1 (compile) → tier2 (JS builders/test runners) → tier3 (dev servers, sonarqube-mcp, SonarLint, headless chrome). Critical and unclassified processes are never shed. kernel_steering writes memory.oom.group=0, memory.high=memory_high_pct of max, and oom_score_adj (builds 1000, critical 0) so the kernel's own last resort also picks a build, never a conductor or an agent.

io._comment: I/O guard policy (.claude/hooks/cargo-disk-guard.py rules 3-5). Evidence 2026-08-29: the control-plane host (ethosengine, the only k8s node) hard-reset twice (12:44Z, 20:53Z) with psi_io some=77%, 45 D-state procs, md2 queue depth 218-277 at 155ms write latency on two Crucial P1 QLC NVMes at 108%/130% of rated TBW; the same day this workspace pod wrote 30G in its first 55 min (45% of the host's writes) and the host's idle write floor is ~13MB/s (~1.1TB/day: alpha peer pods ~8, containerd stdout logs ~2.2, dqlite ~1.6, local mesh ~1-3). Builds are the bursts that push the md queue over; concurrent builds are the proximate trigger. Thresholds read the HOST's /proc/pressure/io (visible in-pod). psi_full_avg10: share of the last 10s ALL tasks were stalled on I/O; psi_some_avg60: share of the last 60s ANY task was. max_concurrent_heavy=1 means one cargo build/test/check (or `just gate`) per container at a time. default_jobs is the CARGO_BUILD_JOBS the guard demands when the env is absent (devfile.yaml sets it for new workspaces).
io._write_budget_2026_09_03: io-guard (genesis/agentic/bin/io-guard) enforces a continuous budget on top of the admission rules above: host PSI full avg10 is the PRIMARY axis (psi_full_high/hard_pct), the container's cgroup io.stat write rate over window_s is secondary (max over devices — md2 and its two mirror members report the same bytes; the first cut summed them and read 3x). CORRECTION 2026-09-03 evening (operator's cluster read): the day's pod swap was not a write storm — the secretless ReplicaSet was rendered 07:21Z during a k8s-dqlite SEGV crash loop and the 10:20Z swap was the Deployment flipping onto that stale template; sysstat had the disk at 8-12 MB/s, <1 ms await at 07:07 and 67 MB/s at 10:21. What the record does show is fsync/latency contention (10:13Z await 81 ms, queue 52 at 38 MB/s) on two QLC NVMes past rated TBW, plus the 2026-08-29 hard resets — hence PSI-first. high = PAUSE (SIGSTOP) the top-writing tier-1 compile tree, one per tick; hard = kill tier-1, pause tier-2; critical/unknown never touched; resume oldest-first once under soft for resume_after_s; dwell resets on daemon start.
io._dont_restrain_by_accident: Operator ruling 2026-09-03: manage carrying capacity as a VSM discipline, but never restrain ourselves on a number the disk does not feel. So: action_level is host PSI only (rate_action=false; the byte rate is advisory in status/ledger); no action unless OUR writes are >= write_min_actionable_mb_s (pausing our compile when someone else is the writer relieves nothing); pause before kill — kill only after kill_after_s of hard dwell when pausing did not relieve the host.

berth._comment: Carrying capacity of THIS workspace as one tevah berth (genesis/agentic/bin/berth). Sessions moor (who: session, model, lab, runtime, principal; what: task, write_set), claim/release leases on the named resources, and leave deliberation notes on the record. Records are Ephemeral (C) locally and shaped for their protocol homes: mooring → delegates-compute Mishpat::Commitment, lease → REA `use` commitment, note → witnessed interaction, shed → tevah §5.3 breach event. capacity 1 = one holder at a time; a second claimant is REFUSED (exit 3) with the holder named, never queued.
